explain.say: In October 1922 tens of thousands of Benito Mussolini's Blackshirts converged on Rome. The army could have stopped them, but King Victor Emmanuel the Third refused to declare martial law and invited Mussolini to form a government. Fascism takes its name from the fasces, the ancient Roman bundle of rods. Look at the timeline.

explain.say: Now the map. Fascism began in Milan in 1919. In Munich in 1923 Adolf Hitler tried a coup, the Beer Hall Putsch; it failed and he went to prison. He decided to win power through elections instead, and then destroy democracy from inside. Why might a legal road be more dangerous than a coup?

See the causes. Bitterness after the war, fear of communist revolution, weak coalition governments, and from 1930 the Depression. Crucially, conservative elites, the king in Italy and President Hindenburg's circle in Germany, believed they could use fascists to crush the left. Which cause do you think mattered most in Germany?

explain.say: Here are real election results. The Nazis won 2.6 percent in 1928, 18.3 percent in 1930 and 37.3 percent in July 1932, then fell to 33.1 percent in November. They never won a majority in a free election. In January 1933 Hindenburg appointed Hitler chancellor in a backroom deal. Spot the dip just before he got power.

After the Reichstag fire, in March 1933 the Enabling Act let Hitler make laws without parliament, passed 444 to 94 while communist deputies were barred and arrested; only the Social Democrats voted no. Now see two definitions: Roger Griffin's myth of national rebirth, Robert Paxton's focus on what fascists did. Excellent. Exam tip: compare Italy and Germany step by step.

faq.a: A far-right movement and form of rule born in Italy in 1919: extreme nationalism, a cult of the leader, violence against opponents, rejection of democracy and communism, and a promise of national rebirth. Roger Griffin stresses the rebirth myth; Robert Paxton stresses what fascists did and their alliances with conservative elites.
asks: Where does the word fascism come from?

faq.q: How did Hitler come to power?
faq.a: The Nazis became the largest party in July 1932 with 37.3 percent but never won a free majority. Conservative politicians around President Hindenburg persuaded him to appoint Hitler chancellor on 30 January 1933, believing they could control him.

faq.q: Why did people vote for the Nazis?
faq.a: Voters were drawn by fear of communism, anger at Versailles, the Depression's mass unemployment, distrust of weak coalition governments, Nazi propaganda and promises of national revival. Support was strongest among Protestant, rural and middle-class voters.

faq.q: What was the March on Rome?
faq.a: In October 1922 Fascist squads converged on Rome. Rather than use the army, King Victor Emmanuel III invited Mussolini to become prime minister, and he built a dictatorship by 1925.

A law of 23 March 1933 letting Hitler's government make laws without the Reichstag. It passed 444 to 94 amid intimidation, with communist deputies barred; only the Social Democrats voted against. It became the legal basis of the dictatorship.
asks: How did Hitler become a dictator?

facts: Mussolini became Italy's prime minister in October 1922.
The Nazis won 37.3 percent of the vote in July 1932.
Hitler was appointed chancellor on 30 January 1933.

quiz.say: The Nazi vote rose from 18.3 percent in 1930 to 37.3 percent in July 1932. By how many percentage points?
quiz.why: 37.3 minus 18.3 equals 19 percentage points: the share roughly doubled.

wrong.1: Nine points would give only about 27 percent.
wrong.2: 37 points is the whole July 1932 share, not the rise.
